task.title: score line formatter
task.statement:
This function turns (name, score) pairs into display lines like "ana: 10". It indexes the list by position and pokes into each pair with [0] and [1] — classic Java reflexes.

    def format_scores(pairs):
        lines = []
        for i in range(len(pairs)):
            pair = pairs[i]
            name = pair[0]
            score = pair[1]
            lines.append(name + ": " + str(score))
        return lines

Rewrite it idiomatically in solution.py; same name, same behavior.
task.notes: Micro-drill. If they ask whether an approach 'counts', say idiomatic means what a fluent reviewer would write today; no other resolutions to give. Targets: index-loop, pair-not-unpacked.
task.appendix:
Targets: index-loop, pair-not-unpacked

Hidden checks (behavior must be preserved):
assert format_scores([("ana", 10), ("bo", 7)]) == ["ana: 10", "bo: 7"]
assert format_scores([]) == []
assert format_scores([["cy", 0]]) == ["cy: 0"]
assert format_scores([("z", -3), ("z", -3)]) == ["z: -3", "z: -3"]

Idiomatic reference:
def format_scores(pairs):
    return [f"{name}: {score}" for name, score in pairs]
